R0288.title: Ticket Scalping and Resale Risk
R0288.definition: Attackers profit by capturing, hoarding, transferring, or reselling tickets, appointment slots, transport seats, and similar scarce ticketed resources at inflated prices.
R0288.description:
Ticket scalping and resale risk occurs in scarce-resource allocation scenarios such as concerts, sports events, attractions, flights, rail tickets, medical appointments, activity reservations, and platform benefit claims. Attackers may use human proxy buying, bulk accounts, automation scripts, proxy IPs, SMS receiving platforms, or secondary-market channels to capture ticketed resources and then profit through markups, proxy orders, transfer codes, account delivery, or fake-ticket transactions.

This risk does not require automated purchasing. It applies whenever attackers exploit scarcity, weak identity verification, poor resale controls, or off-platform trading chains, causing legitimate users to lose fair access, platform order to be disrupted, or consumers to suffer inflated prices and failed entry.
R0288.influence: It concentrates scarce ticketed resources, makes legitimate purchasing difficult, inflates secondary-market prices, increases complaints and regulatory pressure, and can lead to fake-ticket fraud, account-transfer disputes, and failed-entry losses.
